    - heading "Understand Concurrency Test" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A concurrency test checks whether three or more lines pass through one point. In Concurrency Test, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Common point: L1 cap L2 cap L3 = P. You can learn Concurrency Test by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: Construct the lines. Find intersections. Check whether all lines pass through the same point. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
    - paragraph: "In real life, triangle medians: Medians are concurrent at the centroid. Watch out: Checking only two lines. Concurrency for three lines needs all three through one point."

    - heading "Ceva’s Theorem" [level=2]
    - paragraph: For D on BC, E on CA, and F on AB, cevians AD, BE, CF are concurrent if and only if
    - strong: AF/FB × BD/DC × CE/EA = 1
    - paragraph: For exterior points, use directed ratios consistently.

    - text: Product equals 1 ⇒ Concurrent

    - text: Using absolute lengths for exterior side points.
    - paragraph: Signed ratios keep the theorem valid when a point lies on an extension. Keep numerator and denominator order consistent.
